steps.calloutTitle: PCAF data quality — computed per loan
steps.calloutText: PCAF Global GHG Standard Part A 3rd Edition — every loan gets a Score 1-5 based on the data available, not a portfolio average.
steps.narration: This is the PCAF data quality panel on the NFRS tab. PCAF is the Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financials. Its Global GHG Standard Part A defines a 1-to-5 data quality scale for financed emissions. 1 is best, 5 is worst. Every loan in the bank's book gets scored individually based on what data is available for that specific borrower. This is what the CFO and CRO show the auditor when NFRS goes live.

steps.calloutText: 5 loans at Score 1 · 39 at Score 2 · 991 at Score 3 · 79,000 at Score 5. The right-hand tail matters — it is where the audit risk lives.
steps.narration: Here is the actual distribution across an 80,000-loan portfolio. Five loans at Score 1 where the borrower publishes verified GHG-Protocol emissions. Thirty-nine loans at Score 2 with unverified borrower emissions. Roughly a thousand loans at Score 3. computed from physical activity data multiplied by a sector emission factor. That's the slice where Jana's Climate TRACE and Global Cement Tracker data does the work. Seventy-nine thousand loans at Score 5. mostly retail plus SME loans with no facility-level attribution. This distribution replaces the industry-standard practice of averaging one number across the whole book.

steps.calloutText: Score 3 · Option 2b (physical activity × sector emission factor) · citation to PCAF Part A §5.3
steps.narration: Let's drill into a single loan. Hongshi-Shivam Cement. The compliance workbench shows two PCAF panels for this loan. The lower panel — data quality for this loan — shows the computed score. Above it, the PCAF Data Availability panel — where the analyst confirms what data actually exists for this borrower. That is the panel we walk through next.

steps.calloutText: Auto-inference from the borrower record is the starting point. The officer confirms or overrides each flag with evidence.
steps.narration: This is the PCAF Data Availability panel. Every borrower gets four flag rows corresponding to the PCAF option ladder. Verified reported emissions. Unverified reported. Physical activity data. Revenue-only. The starting state is auto-inferred from what the bank's borrower record contains. Riya then confirms or overrides each one before the score becomes defensible for filing.

steps.calloutTitle: Four flag rows · one for each PCAF option
steps.calloutText: Verified · Unverified · Physical activity · Revenue-only. Higher flag ON = higher option in the ladder.
steps.narration: Four flag rows on this panel. Each row corresponds to one option in the PCAF ladder. Verified reported emissions moves the loan to Score 1 Option 1a. Unverified reported moves it to Score 2. Physical activity data available moves it to Score 3 Option 2b — that is the row where Jana's Climate TRACE and Global Cement Tracker data does the work. Revenue-only is the fallback that puts the loan at Score 4. When Riya toggles a flag away from the auto-inferred state, the badge flips from AUTO to OVERRIDE so the audit trail records who changed what.

steps.calloutTitle: Evidence field · what the auditor sees
steps.calloutText: URL to the sustainability report, page range, verifier name, dated snapshot. Auditors read this before they read the score.
steps.narration: The evidence field is what makes this defensible. On Hongshi, the seeded evidence references the 2024 Sustainability and GHG Report pages 42 to 46, plus the KPMG assurance opinion under ISAE 3410. When the NFRS auditor asks how you got to Score 1, you point at this field. Same story for every borrower in the bank's book. Save the panel and the PCAF score below re-computes with the new inputs immediately.

steps.calloutText: Business loans · project finance · mortgages · motor vehicles · listed equity · corporate bonds · sovereign debt · commercial real estate · sub-sovereign · securitisation.
steps.narration: PCAF 3rd Edition expanded to ten asset classes. Business loans, project finance, motor vehicle loans, mortgages, listed equity, corporate bonds, sovereign debt, commercial real estate, and two newer categories added in the 2025 edition. sub-sovereign debt and securitisation. Every loan in the bank's book maps to one of these classes and the scoring rubric adjusts accordingly. project finance uses a slightly different option list than business loans, and sovereign debt uses country-level data rather than facility-level. The scoring engine handles the differences automatically.

steps.calloutTitle: Score 3 is the honest ceiling · with Jana
steps.calloutText: Score 1-2 require borrower disclosure. Score 3 is the realistic ceiling for Nepal facilities. Score 5 is the baseline everyone else operates at.
steps.narration: The takeaway for a Nepal bank. Score 1 or 2 requires the borrower to publish their own GHG Protocol emissions. Almost no Nepal special-purpose vehicle does that today. Score 3 is the honest ceiling with Jana's data on the loans that carry the emissions risk. And without Jana the whole book collapses to Score 5. revenue-based estimates using national averages. When NFRS goes live and NRB or an auditor asks for the distribution, this is the picture the bank shows. Thanks for watching.
